festivals: Pran Pratishtha / consecration anniversary (1-4 December, four-day event)

history.summary: The Sai Baba Temple on Wardha Road, Vivekanand Nagar, Nagpur is a modern temple built on the model of the Shirdi Samadhi Mandir. The idea originated at the older Shri Sai Mandir in Dhantoli; a trust was formed in 1971 and registered in 1972. Land was purchased from Shri Banerjee in 1974 and bhoomipujan performed in 1976; funds were raised through donations and cultural programmes (notably a free performance by Pt. Bhimsen Joshi and a fundraiser featuring Dilip Kumar). The temple, designed by architect Shri Shivdanmal, was completed in 1979, and the marble idol (donated by Shri Babulalji Warti, sculpted by Talim of Mumbai) was consecrated 1-4 December 1979 by Godavari Mata of Sakori. It draws large Thursday crowds.

name: Sai Baba Temple
town_description: Nagpur, the 'Orange City' of Maharashtra, is the largest city of the Vidarbha region and a major commercial, transport and political centre of central India. It is known for its oranges, for Deekshabhoomi (the Buddhist stupa of Ambedkar's mass conversion), and for the Zero Mile marker said to mark the geographical centre of India. The Sai Baba Temple stands on Wardha Road near the airport, in the southern part of the city.
tradition: Hinduism (Sai Baba devotion; all religions welcome)
